To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the indirect detection signatures of decaying ADM can be used to probe the origin of the primordial DM asymmetry.

(1) the decay of light ADM is constrained by gamma-ray and antiproton fluxes, (2) heavy ADM is constrained by γ-ray and e+/e− fluxes, (3) the best fit regions for heavy ADM from e+/e− measurement are in tension with other constraints, and (4) decaying ADM with a primordial abundance is more consistent with the data than symmetric DM.

the decay signatures of ADM are sensitive to the nature of higher dimension operator generating DM asymmetry and the sign of the lepton/baryon number that the DM particle carries, and the current constraints from the indirect detection experiments can be evaded by a proper choice of the higher dimension operators and the DM mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism to generate the DM asymmetry in a natural way and we have shown that indirect detection of ADM can be used to constrain this mechanism.
a systematic study of the indirect detection signals from the decay of asymmetric dark matter in the context of a minimal model.
indirect detection of decaying dark matter with a primordial asymmetric origin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the decay of DM is still viable as an explanation for the signals, a more precise measurement is necessary.

the decay of ADM is not excluded as a source of the signals, and that it may even explain the signals better than a symmetric DM scenario, although the best-fit region is still in tension with the data.
indirect detection of decaying dark matter with a primordial abundance can not be excluded by current data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decaying DM scenario is not ruled out by current indirect detection experiments, but it is not favored over the symmetric dark matter scenario either.
the decay of asymmetric dark matter can be constrained by indirect detection experiments, but the tension among the measurements is not yet solved.
indirect detection of decaying DM can be a powerful tool for studying the origin of the DM asymmetry, but the current data are still insufficient for a definite conclusion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
indirect detection can probe the nature of the DM asymmetry generating operators.
indirect detection may provide us with a window into the origin of the dark matter asymmetry.
the decay of ADM is a very promising channel to probe the mechanism that generates the primordial asymmetry.
